rules: Gold, Deluxe and Ultimate labels do not prove a physical SKU.
A SteelBook can be a bonus item without a game.
Collector packaging does not prove that physical game media is included.
Preorder pages, store IDs and mockups do not prove a released physical product.
Code-in-box, Game-Key Card, download-required media and full physical game are distinct products.
Compilation components can mix physical media and vouchers.
Retailer bundles are not automatically publisher editions.
Outer product identifiers must remain separate from inner game identifiers.
A platform identifier incompatible with the target platform is a blocking conflict.

ps5: Start with Ubisoft and PlayStation identity pages, then DoesItPlay for media/install claims, then exact retail or specimen evidence.
ds: Prioritize Nintendo product codes and component-bound DBox, OGDB or Retroplace images; keep box and cartridge codes separate.
wiiu: Treat collector-edition outer packaging separately from the standard inner game; require Skull Edition binding on every claim.
switch: Distinguish game card, code-in-box and download-required content; product code and download statement need component evidence.
xbox360: Model compilation outer barcode, each inner game and standalone releases as separate identities; reject incompatible platform identifiers.
